title: Chevening Scholarships
summary: UK government scholarships for one-year master's degrees at UK universities, for future leaders from Chevening-eligible countries, including Ghana.
description: Chevening is the UK government's international scholarships programme. Awards are for a one-year taught master's degree at an eligible UK university. Selection focuses on leadership potential and professional experience, and scholars are expected to return home after their studies.
fundingCoverage: Additional allowances as set by Chevening
eligibility: Citizen of a Chevening-eligible country (Ghana is listed)
Commit to return to your country of citizenship for at least two years after the award ends
Hold an undergraduate degree that allows entry to a UK postgraduate programme
Have at least two years (2,800 hours) of work experience
Apply to three different eligible UK courses and hold an unconditional offer from one of them by the stated deadline
applicationInstructions: Apply online through the official Chevening website during the application window.
Apply separately to your chosen UK universities; you must secure an unconditional offer by the Chevening offer deadline (reported as 8 July 2027 for the 2027/28 cycle).
Shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview.
deadlineNote: Reported for the 2027/28 cycle (closing 11:00 UTC). Not yet confirmed on the official Chevening website.

title: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
summary: Funded master's study in the UK for candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries, including Ghana. Applicants must be nominated by a national nominating agency.
description: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships are funded by the UK government and managed by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC). They support students from eligible Commonwealth countries whose study will contribute to development in their home country.
eligibility: Citizen of, or refugee from, an eligible Commonwealth country, and permanently resident there
Hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours standard, or a lower second-class degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification
Unable to afford to study in the UK without the scholarship
applicationInstructions: You must be nominated by an approved nominating agency in Ghana. Contact the agency first — its internal deadline may be earlier than the CSC deadline.
Complete your application in the CSC online application system before the deadline.
deadlineNote: Reported CSC closing date for the 2027/28 cycle (16:00 BST). Nominating-agency deadlines in Ghana may be earlier. Not yet confirmed on the official CSC website.

title: Rhodes Scholarship for West Africa
summary: Postgraduate study at the University of Oxford for outstanding young people from West African countries, including Ghana.
description: The Rhodes Scholarship funds postgraduate study at the University of Oxford. A small number of scholarships are allocated to the West Africa constituency each year.
eligibleCountries: Other West African countries in the constituency
fundingCoverage: Economy travel to and from Oxford
eligibility: Citizen of (or resident in) a country in the West Africa constituency, which includes Ghana
Age, degree and residency requirements are set out in the official 'Information for Candidates' document for West Africa
requirements: References written in English, submitted by the reference deadline
applicationInstructions: Read the West Africa 'Information for Candidates' document on the Rhodes Trust website.
Apply online through the Rhodes Trust application system before the closing date.
deadlineNote: Reported closing date (23:59 GMT) for October 2027 entry; references reportedly due 3 September 2026. Not yet confirmed on the official Rhodes Trust website.

title: Mandela Rhodes Scholarship
summary: Postgraduate scholarships (Honours or Master's) at South African universities for young African leaders, combined with a leadership development programme.
fundingCoverage: Tuition for a one-year Honours or two-year Master's degree
eligibility: Citizen of an African country
Planning Honours or Master's study at a recognised South African higher education institution
Able to study in English
applicationInstructions: Apply online through the Mandela Rhodes Foundation website when applications open.
deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027 cohort were reported to have closed on 14 April 2026. The next cycle's dates have not been confirmed.

title: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship
summary: Hungarian government scholarships for bachelor's, master's and doctoral study in Hungary for students from partner countries. Ghana is reported to be a partner country.
eligibility: Citizen of a Stipendium Hungaricum partner country (Ghana is reported to be one)
Nominated by the sending partner (the responsible authority) in your home country
Meet the admission requirements of the chosen Hungarian university programme
applicationInstructions: Apply in the official Stipendium Hungaricum online application system.
Also complete the separate application process of the sending partner in Ghana — its procedures and deadlines may differ.
deadlineNote: Reported deadline for the 2026/27 intake (2 p.m. CET). Dates for the next intake have not been confirmed.

title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
provider: Gates Cambridge Trust, University of Cambridge
summary: Full-cost scholarships for outstanding applicants from any country outside the UK to pursue a full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge.
eligibleCountries: Any country outside the United Kingdom (including Ghana)
fundingCoverage: Full cost of study at Cambridge (fees and maintenance), as defined by the Gates Cambridge Trust
eligibility: Citizen of any country outside the UK
Applying to a full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge
applicationInstructions: Apply for your Cambridge postgraduate course through the University's graduate application portal and complete the Gates Cambridge section of the funding application.
Submit by your course's funding deadline — for most non-US applicants this is reported to be either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, depending on the course.
deadlineNote: No single deadline: it depends on your Cambridge course's funding deadline (reported as 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 for most non-US applicants). Not yet confirmed on the official website.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at KNUST
provider: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) with the Mastercard Foundation
summary: Comprehensive scholarships for academically qualified young people with financial need to study at KNUST in Kumasi.
eligibility: Valid WASSCE, GBCE, ABCE, GCE O/A Level or equivalent results (previous cycles required results not more than five years old)
Demonstrated financial need
Record of leadership and community engagement
Commitment to giving back to your community
applicationInstructions: Check the KNUST Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program website for the current call for applications and application form.
deadlineNote: The current cycle's deadline has not been confirmed. The previous (2025/26) cycle reportedly closed on 30 June 2025.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Ashesi University
provider: Ashesi University with the Mastercard Foundation
summary: Scholarships for academically talented African students with financial need to study at Ashesi University in Berekuso, Ghana.
fundingCoverage: Study resources, including books and a laptop
eligibility: Citizen of an African country
Excellent academic record
Demonstrated financial need
Leadership potential and commitment to community service
applicationInstructions: Apply for admission to Ashesi University through its online portal and complete the scholarship application included in the admission process.
deadlineNote: The current cycle's deadline has not been confirmed. A previous cycle reportedly closed on 14 June 2025.

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships
summary: EU-funded scholarships for integrated master's programmes delivered by consortia of universities in two or more European countries. Open to students worldwide.
description: Each Erasmus Mundus Joint Master is run by a consortium of universities that sets its own admission requirements and deadlines. There is no single central application.
eligibility: Hold a first higher-education degree or equivalent, and meet the chosen programme's admission requirements
Scholarship eligibility may be restricted if you have recently lived in Erasmus+ programme countries for an extended period — check the rules of the programme you apply to
applicationInstructions: Choose a programme from the Erasmus Mundus catalogue.
Apply directly to that programme's consortium through its own website and deadline.
deadlineNote: Deadlines vary by programme and are set by each consortium, typically several months before the intake.

title: Fulbright Foreign Student Program (Ghana)
provider: U.S. Department of State, administered by the U.S. Embassy in Ghana
summary: Funding for up to two years of master's or doctoral study in the United States for Ghanaian staff, junior faculty and administrators at tertiary, research or government institutions.
fundingCoverage: Funding toward a master's or doctoral degree in the United States for up to two years (see the embassy announcement for what is covered)
eligibility: Ghanaian citizen currently residing in Ghana (dual U.S. citizens are not eligible)
Employed at a tertiary, research or government institution
Pursuing study or research in one of the priority fields listed by the embassy for this cycle
applicationInstructions: Read the current call on the U.S. Embassy in Ghana website.
Apply online through the Foreign Fulbright application system before the national deadline.
deadlineNote: Reported national deadline for the 2027–2028 cycle (5 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time). Not yet confirmed on the official embassy page.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
summary: Funded full-time doctoral study at a UK university for candidates from eligible Commonwealth countries, including Ghana. Applicants must be nominated by a national nominating agency.
eligibility: Citizen of, or refugee from, an eligible Commonwealth country, and permanently resident there
Unable to afford to study in the UK without the scholarship
Meet the academic requirements for UK doctoral study
applicationInstructions: You must be nominated by an approved nominating agency in Ghana. Contact the agency first — its internal deadline may be earlier than the CSC deadline.
Complete your application in the CSC online application system before the deadline.
deadlineNote: Reported CSC closing date for study starting in 2027. Nominating-agency deadlines in Ghana may be earlier. Not yet confirmed on the official CSC website.

title: DAAD EPOS: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses
summary: Scholarships for professionals from developing and emerging countries to take selected development-related master's (and some PhD) courses at German universities.
eligibleCountries: Other eligible developing and emerging countries
fundingCoverage: Monthly stipend, insurance and travel allowance as set by DAAD for the course
eligibility: Citizen of a country on the DAAD EPOS list of eligible countries
Bachelor's degree (usually four years) in a relevant subject
At least two years of professional experience
Language requirements set by the chosen course
applicationInstructions: Choose a course from the official DAAD EPOS list for the current intake.
Apply directly to that course — each has its own application process and deadline.
deadlineNote: No single deadline: each participating course sets its own. For courses starting in 2027, deadlines are reported to fall mostly between 1 October and 15 December 2026.

title: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals
summary: Scholarships for full-time master's studies in Sweden for professionals from eligible countries, including Ghana.
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible country (Ghana is listed)
Work experience requirement (reported as at least 3,000 hours) — check the exact rules for the current cycle
Admitted to an eligible master's programme in Sweden
applicationInstructions: Apply for an eligible master's programme through University Admissions in Sweden.
Then apply for the scholarship through the Swedish Institute before its deadline.
deadlineNote: Reported scholarship deadline for the 2027 cycle. University admission deadlines come earlier. Not yet confirmed on the official website.

title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program
provider: World Bank, funded by the Government of Japan
summary: Master's scholarships in development-related fields for mid-career professionals from developing countries, including Ghana.
eligibleCountries: Other eligible World Bank member developing countries
fundingCoverage: Other associated costs as set by the program
eligibility: National of an eligible developing country, without dual citizenship of a developed country
Bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline
Employed full-time in development-related work, generally with at least three years of such experience
Unconditionally admitted to a participating master's programme
applicationInstructions: Secure admission to one of the participating master's programmes.
Apply through the World Bank scholarship portal during one of the application windows.
deadlineNote: Reported 2027 windows: 18 January–26 February 2027 and 29 March–21 May 2027. Not yet confirmed on the official World Bank page.

title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship — Research Students
provider: Government of Japan (MEXT), via the Embassy of Japan in Ghana
summary: Scholarships for Ghanaians to pursue master's or doctoral study at Japanese graduate schools, including an initial period of Japanese language study.
fundingCoverage: Scholarship support for 18 months to two years, including up to six months of Japanese language study (see the official guidelines for allowances)
eligibility: Ghanaian citizen
Age limit applies (for the 2027 intake, born on or after 2 April 1992)
Willing to learn Japanese
Meets the academic requirements in the official application guidelines
applicationInstructions: Download the application guidelines and forms from the Study in Japan website.
Submit the completed forms as instructed in the Embassy of Japan in Ghana announcement.
deadlineNote: The 2027 intake reportedly closed on 29 May 2026. Dates for the next cycle have not been confirmed.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (Bilateral Program)
provider: Government of China (China Scholarship Council), via the Chinese Embassy in Ghana
summary: Chinese government scholarships for Ghanaian students to study in China, offered through the embassy (bilateral) channel.
eligibility: Ghanaian citizen
Meets the admission requirements of the chosen Chinese university
applicationInstructions: Check the official Campus China website for universities and programs.
Obtain any required pre-admission documents from your chosen university.
Apply online and follow the Chinese Embassy in Ghana's instructions for the bilateral program.
deadlineNote: The current cycle's deadline has not been confirmed. The previous cycle's online deadline was reported to be in mid-February.

title: Australia Awards Africa — Master's Scholarships
provider: Australian Government (Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade)
summary: Scholarships for mid-career professionals from eligible African countries, including Ghana, to complete a master's degree in Australia.
fundingCoverage: See the official intake profile for what the scholarship covers
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible African country (Ghana is listed)
Minimum age and work-experience requirements set out in the official intake profile
Employed at the time of applying
applicationInstructions: Read the Africa intake profile and eligibility page on the Australia Awards Africa website.
Apply online when the application round opens.
deadlineNote: The next round is reported to open from 1 February 2027. The closing date has not been confirmed.

title: Ghana Scholarships Authority — Local Tertiary Scholarship
summary: Government scholarship for academically gifted but financially challenged Ghanaian students admitted to accredited tertiary institutions in Ghana.
eligibility: Ghanaian citizen with a valid Ghana Card
Admitted to an accredited tertiary institution in Ghana
Academically strong with financial need
applicationInstructions: Apply online through the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal during the application window and upload the required documents.
The Authority states its services are free and no third party is engaged to assist applicants.
deadlineNote: The 2026/2027 window was reported as 20 April–20 May 2026. Dates for the next intake have not been confirmed.

title: GNPC Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
summary: Limited undergraduate scholarships for Ghanaian students at accredited tertiary institutions in Ghana.
eligibility: Ghanaian first-year or continuing student at an accredited tertiary institution in Ghana
Not already a beneficiary of another scholarship scheme
First-year applicants: credit passes in six WASSCE/SSSCE subjects, including core subjects (as reported)
applicationInstructions: Check the GNPC Foundation website for the current call and apply through its official application portal.
deadlineNote: A 31 December 2026 deadline for 2026/2027 was reported by third-party sites. Not yet confirmed by GNPC.
